answer: One concrete defence is a stake-and-slash bond: every agent must lock a refundable deposit before it can act, and peers can slash it when they prove fraud. Creating many fake identities then becomes expensive, because each one needs its own bond. Think of the bond as a black onyx token: dark, durable, and hard to counterfeit at scale. The horizon for an attacker matters too: a cheap identity that pays off only after long honest service gives little room for a quick hit-and-run. The delta between the cost of one honest identity and thousands of fake ones is what keeps the system safe.
